title: Station events post
description: The body of POST /api/station/events, as the station sends it today (StationLink._forward, sizeup/cloud/station.py): the oldest rows of its outbox, in order. Everything the station hears that must not be lost goes this way: pages, transmissions with their clips, new words, radio ids, the incident sources' events. Plain JSON, never gzipped, with a Content-Length; the hub takes at most 32 MiB. A batch is the oldest rows up to 200 events and 4 MiB of data and clips before base64, and always at least one (so one event over 4 MiB goes alone). The hub answers `station-events-answer` with its cursor, and the station then deletes every row up to it; on any other answer it sends the same batch again. Delivery is at least once and in order: the cursor rules are in contracts/README.md and contracts/events/cursor.json. Times are Unix seconds, never milliseconds.

epoch.description: The outbox's identity: 16 lower-case hex characters made at random with the outbox file (Outbox, sizeup/cloud/outbox.py). The hub's cursor counts within one epoch: a post with another epoch than the last one's sets the cursor to 0 and everything in it is applied. So a new outbox file must have a new epoch, and two writers must never share a hub with one each. The hub cuts it to 40 characters and takes a missing one as "".

station.description: The station's id, as the hub last named it (else its config's). The hub checks it against the token: another station's id is 401 `id_mismatch`. It keys nothing by it: the cursor is the hub's one, whoever posts. "" from a station with no id of its own.

events.description: The events, oldest first (the hub sorts them by `seq` before it applies them). The station never posts an empty list; the hub takes one and answers its cursor. The hub answers 400 when this is not a list.

event.title: One event
event.description: One row of the station's outbox (sizeup/cloud/outbox.py). An item of `events` that is not an object is not applied and is listed under `rejected` as `malformed` (#762).

seq.description: The row's number in the outbox: 1 for the first event of an epoch, strictly increasing, never used twice within an epoch (not even after the row is gone). The hub's cursor is the highest `seq` of the epoch it has dealt with: an event at or under it is skipped as delivered before. A gap is not noticed.

at.description: When the station queued it, Unix seconds. Sent, never read by the hub.

type.description: What the event is: it picks the shape of `data`. The hub logs and acks a type it does not know, and applies nothing.

audio.description: The event's clip: a whole RIFF / WAVE file in base64 (RFC 4648 section 4: the standard alphabet, with padding, no line breaks), so it always starts `UklGR`. null for an event without a clip and for one whose clip the outbox dropped. The station sends PCM, mono, 16-bit, 8000 frames a second (its 16 kHz clip, every other sample). The hub checks none of that: it decodes the base64 without validation and stores the bytes as they are.

audio_dropped.description: The outbox dropped this event's clip to stay under its size cap (`audio` is then null). Sent, never read by the hub.

qid.description: Present only on a copy of an event the hub refused that the station's quarantine sends again (sizeup/cloud/outbox.py requeue_due, #762): the quarantine row's id. The hub reads it on a `source_event` only (#791): it marks that snapshot `resent`, and a re-sent snapshot older than the one it applied is dropped, however small the gap (a first send keeps the 120 s tolerance). The hub's cursor treats the copy as any event (a new `seq`).

clip_id.description: A clip id: a letter or digit, then at most 120 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, never two dots in a row. The hub fails the event for any other id.

page.title: page: a page off the air
page.description: A page (or a voice transmission) on a paging channel, the moment its recording is complete and before its transcript (App._page_done, sizeup/app.py). Its `audio` is the clip. The `page_text` of the same id follows.

page_text.title: page_text: a page's transcript
page_text.description: The same page again once speech-to-text is done with it (App._transcribed_one, sizeup/app.py): the whole document, now with `raw`, `confidence`, `status`, `model` and `dispatch`. No `audio`. The hub reads `raw`, `confidence`, `status`, `model`, `stt` and `vocab_v` from it; when it never had the `page`, it takes the whole document as the page. It ignores one for a page that is already final.

traffic.title: traffic: a finished transmission
traffic.description: A finished transmission with its clip, once speech-to-text is done with it or was not asked (App._transcribed_one, sizeup/app.py). The transmission's own keys; beside the ten it always has, `raw`, `confidence`, `model`, `stt`, `attach` and `pairs` are always there. Its `audio` is the clip.

alarm.title: alarm: an emergency button, ahead of the words
alarm.description: The emergency button, sent the moment it is known and before speech-to-text (App._alarm_now, sizeup/app.py): the transmission as it is then, so without the keys speech-to-text adds and without `attach`; `pairs` is always a list. Its `audio` is the clip when there is one yet (none for an alarm raised at the key-up of an FM carrier). The `traffic` event of the same id follows with the words. A flag the station found stuck is sent once as an alarm with `emergency` false and `flag_stuck`. The hub stores the clip unless it has it, clears `text`, and raises or updates the alarm.

pairs.description: An alarm's `pairs` is always a list ([] when it has none), never null.

retext.title: retext: new words for a clip
retext.description: New words for a page or a transmission the hub already has: a re-run on the station, the station's whisper standing in for Amazon Transcribe, or a shed clip caught up (App._retext, sizeup/app.py). No `audio`.

id.description: The clip the words are for. An id the hub does not know changes nothing.

text.description: The new words; "" when nothing was said.

status.description: Its speech-to-text status now. The hub takes a missing one as `done`.

confidence.description: The model's confidence, 0 to 1; null without one.

model.description: The model that wrote the words.

stt_prompt_time.description: Present (true) only when whisper's prompt carried the clip's own time.

alt.title: The other engine's words
alt.description: The other engine's transcript, kept to compare. Present only on a re-run that has one.

catchup.description: Present (true) only for a shed clip caught up later: the words may be hours old, so on the hub nothing that alerts hears them.

vocab_v.description: The version of the term list that went into whisper's prompt. Present only when one did. The hub cuts it to 80 characters.

late.description: Present (true) only for the words of a P25 call written while sizeup was down and ingested at its next start (#747): on the hub nothing that pre-alerts hears them; an emergency still alarms, labelled late.

rerun.title: rerun: a re-run is over
rerun.description: A re-run of a clip's speech-to-text on the station ended (App._rerun_finish, sizeup/app.py). No `audio`.

id.description: The clip that was run again.

result.description: `changed`, `same` or `failed: <why>`, then notes after `; ` (`changed; catch-up`); at most 300 characters. The hub keeps the first 200.

model.description: The model that ran; "" when none did. The hub keeps the first 80 characters.

alt_text.title: alt_text: the other engine's words
alt_text.description: The station's whisper text as the alternative to the text of record (a re-run with both engines; App._set_alt, sizeup/app.py). No `audio`.

id.description: The clip the alternative is for.

model.description: The model that wrote them. The hub keeps the first 80 characters.

heard.title: heard: a radio id on the air
heard.description: A radio id heard on the air, for the hub's radio registry (App._heard, sizeup/app.py). Sent at most once per (system, radio id, alias) in 300 s. No `audio`.

system.description: The signalling the id came in. The hub ignores the event, without a word, for any other value.

radio_id.description: The radio id as decoded: P25 unit id (digits), MDC-1200 (4 hex), FleetSync (`<fleet>-<id>`). Never "".

alias.description: The alias the P25 system sent for it; "" when none.

at.description: When it was heard, Unix seconds; null when not known.

channel.description: The channel's label or the talkgroup's name it was heard on.

activity.title: activity: a minute of key-ups on an encrypted talkgroup
activity.description: A minute's key-ups on an encrypted talkgroup of another P25 system: counted, never recorded (App._p25_activity, sizeup/app.py). Context: the station holds it back from a hub that has not said `p25_systems` in its `caps`. No `audio`.

minute.description: Which minute: Unix time divided by 60, whole.

calls.description: How many key-ups in that minute.

radios.description: The radio ids that keyed up. The hub keeps the first 40, each cut to 12 characters.

source_event.title: source_event: an incident source's event
source_event.description: A new or changed event of an external incident source running on the station (sizeup/sources/runner.py). The only event type the hub does not ack when it fails to apply it (see the cursor rules): it is sent again, three deliveries at most. No `audio`.

source.description: The adapter's id: a lower-case letter or digit, then at most 31 of a-z, 0-9, `_`, `-`; never `paging`. The hub fails the event otherwise.

label.description: The adapter's name for people. The hub keeps the first 60 characters.

rank.description: The adapter's rank among the sources, 1 the first. The hub takes anything outside 1 to 99 as 1.

seen_at.description: When the station handed this version on, Unix seconds. From #762 on the hub keeps it with the report and ignores a version more than 120 s older than the one it has applied (one sent again from the station's quarantine).

first_seen.description: When the station first had the event, Unix seconds: the adapter's own time when it gives a believable one, else `seen_at`. The hub takes it as when the report came.

source_health.title: source_health: an incident source's health
source_health.description: How an incident source's adapter is doing: on every change and every 60 s (sizeup/sources/runner.py). The hub keeps the newest by `at`. No `audio`.

source.description: The adapter's id: a lower-case letter or digit, then at most 31 of a-z, 0-9, `_`, `-`; never `paging`. The hub fails the event otherwise.

label.description: The adapter's name for people. The hub keeps the first 60 characters.

rank.description: The adapter's rank among the sources, 1 the first. The hub takes anything outside 1 to 99 as 1.

state.description: The adapter's state. The hub fails the event for a word it does not know.

reason.description: Why, short, for people; "" when ok. At most 200 characters; never a secret, an address of a server or a server's own text.

since.description: When it entered this state, Unix seconds; null when the adapter does not say.

at.description: When the station made this report, Unix seconds. The hub fails the event when it is not a number.

stopped.description: The adapter itself says it has stopped (its own health is `failing`).

source_seen.title: source_seen: the ids an incident source still lists
source_seen.description: The event ids in an incident source's last good snapshot, every 120 s, so the hub can flag an open report the source no longer lists (sizeup/sources/runner.py). No `audio`.

source.description: The adapter's id: a lower-case letter or digit, then at most 31 of a-z, 0-9, `_`, `-`; never `paging`. The hub fails the event otherwise.

label.description: The adapter's name for people. The hub keeps the first 60 characters.

rank.description: The adapter's rank among the sources, 1 the first. The hub takes anything outside 1 to 99 as 1.

at.description: When the station made this list, Unix seconds.

ids.description: The event ids in the snapshot, at most 2000. The hub fails the event when this is not a list.

complete.description: False when the list was cut at 2000: the hub then flags nothing. The hub takes a missing one as true.

page_doc.title: A page
page_doc.description: A page off a paging channel as the station keeps it and sends it (App._page_doc, sizeup/app.py: Page.as_dict of sizeup/radio/page.py plus what the pipeline added). The hub builds its own Page from it (page_from_dict): `id`, `label`, `mhz`, `start`, `end` and `kind` must be there (a missing one fails the event), every other key has a default. The hub does not read `departments`, `read_twice` (it works both out again from `tones` and `raw`), `rerun_result` nor `vocab_v` of a `page` event.

id.description: The page's clip id: 10 hex characters made by the station. The hub ignores a `page` whose id it has already.

start.description: When the recording starts, Unix seconds, two decimals.

end.description: When it ends, Unix seconds, two decimals. The hub files the clip under this time.

status.description: Where its speech-to-text stands. `pending`: the station's whisper has it; `remote`: the hub is to transcribe it (the channel's engine is Amazon Transcribe); `done` / `no_speech`: final; `no_voice`: tones only; `off` / `skipped` / `error`: not transcribed. The hub takes a missing one as `done`.

departments.description: Every name in `tones`, in order, once each. Sent, never read: the hub works it out from `tones`.

quieting_db.description: How far the carrier quieted the hiss, dB, one decimal.

tones.description: The tone pairs decoded, in order; [] for a voice page.

raw.description: The transcript; "" until there is one.

confidence.description: The model's confidence in the transcript, 0 to 1; null without one.

voice_offset_s.description: Where the voice starts in the clip, seconds, three decimals; 0 for a voice page.

dispatch.description: What the station's parser read in `raw`; null before the transcript and when nothing was read.

history.description: The texts it had before, oldest first, at most the last 5.

rerun_at.description: When its text was last written again by a re-run, Unix seconds; null when never.

rerun_result.description: The last re-run's result (see the `rerun` event); "" when none. Sent, never read by the hub from a page.

model.description: The model that wrote `raw`; "" before the transcript.

stt.description: Which engine the hub is to add. "": none (the station's whisper alone); `aws`: the hub transcribes the clip with Amazon Transcribe; `both`: the hub adds Amazon Transcribe's text as the alternative; `pool`: handed to the hub's speech-to-text pool.

read_twice.description: The message was read twice, from the transcript; null for a voice page. Sent, never read: the hub works it out from `raw`.

vocab_v.description: The version of the term list that went into whisper's prompt; "" when none. Read by the hub from a `page_text` only (cut to 80 characters).

alt_text.description: The other engine's transcript. Only with `alt_model`.

alt_model.description: The model that wrote `alt_text`. Present only when there is an alternative; the hub reads `alt_text` only when this is set.

radio_id.description: The radio id(s) decoded on a unit's key-up cut from a page, joined with ", ". Present only when one was decoded.

unit.description: Who keyed that key-up, as the station names them, joined with ", ". Present only with `radio_id`.

tone.title: One tone pair
tone.description: A two-tone pair or a long tone decoded in the page (sizeup/radio/tones.py ToneEvent).

kind.description: The hub fails the event without it.

a_hz.description: The first tone, Hz, one decimal. The hub fails the event without it.

b_hz.description: The second tone, Hz, one decimal; null for a long tone.

items.description: One department's name in the station's tone plan.

names.description: Who the station's tone plan says this pair pages; [] when it names nobody.

start.description: Where the pair starts, seconds into the clip.

end.description: Where the pair ends, seconds into the clip.

tone_heard.title: One tone heard
tone_heard.description: One tone as heard, in order, whether or not it is part of a pair (sizeup/radio/tones.py ToneDetector.sequence).

start.description: Where it starts, seconds into the clip.

role.description: Its place in a pair; "" when it is in none.

dispatch.title: A parsed dispatch
dispatch.description: What the station's parser read in the page's words (sizeup/dispatch.py Dispatch). The hub keeps it on the page as it came and parses the words again itself for the CAD.

text.description: The words it was parsed from.

items.description: One department named in the words.

departments.description: The departments named in the words.

incident_type.description: The type of call, as the parser names it; "" when none was read.

category.description: The type's category, one lower-case word; "" when none.

type_phrase.description: The words that gave the type.

code.description: A priority dispatch code as spoken; "" when none.

numbers.description: Other numbers read in the words.

location.description: The address, lower case as parsed; "" when none.

qualifier.description: From #PRNUM on: where at the location, as said in front of it ("across from"): its location_qualifiers code ("ACROSS"); "" when none. Never part of location.

cross_street.description: The cross street, lower case; "" when none.

time_out.description: The time spoken at the end, HH:MM; "" when none.

earlier_text.title: An earlier text
earlier_text.description: A text this page had before a re-run changed it.

at.description: When it was replaced, Unix seconds.

model.description: The model that wrote the earlier words; "" when not known.

keyup.title: A piece cut at a key-up
keyup.description: A transmission that is a piece of one recording cut at key-ups (sizeup/radio/fm.py, am.py; App.keyup_link): which recording, and the piece before it.

parent.description: The clip id of the recording's first piece (the first piece: its own).

prev.description: The clip id of the piece before this one; "" for the first.

split.description: Why it was cut from the piece before; "" for the first.

transmission.title: A transmission
transmission.description: One finished transmission as the station holds it: every attribute of its Traffic object (sizeup/incidents.py: Traffic.as_dict is the object's whole __dict__ but `raw_audio`). Ten of them are the object's declared fields and are always there; the rest are set along the way by whichever path the transmission took (an FM channel, the airband, a talkgroup of the county P25 system, one of another P25 system, speech-to-text), so most are absent on most transmissions. `x-hub` on each key says what the hub does with it: `required` (the event fails without it), `read` (the hub acts on it by name), `replaced` (the hub writes its own value over it), `kept` (nothing on the hub reads it by name). Whatever it says, the hub KEEPS every key whose name is a lower-case letter followed by at most 30 lower-case letters, digits or underscores, known or not, as an attribute of its own copy, and hands it on to every console in the row; a key with any other name, and `has_audio`, is dropped. So a key added here reaches the consoles the day a station sends it: this list is closed by the tests (`x-complete`), not by the hub.

id.description: The clip id, and the row's id everywhere. An FM or airband channel: `<label without spaces>-<start in ms>`; a P25 call: trunk-recorder's call name, with `-t<k>` when the call has more than one key-up; an alarm raised at the key-up of an FM carrier: `<label without spaces>-live-<start in ms>`. The hub ignores a `traffic` whose id it has already.

source.description: Where it was heard: the channel's label, or the talkgroup's name. The hub fails the event without it, and files the clip under it.

start.description: When it starts, Unix seconds. The hub fails the event without it.

end.description: When it ends, Unix seconds. The hub fails the event without it, and files the clip under this time.

text.description: The words; "" when nothing was said or it was not transcribed. The hub fails the event without it and then writes `raw` over it ("" for an alarm).

status.description: Where its speech-to-text stands. `done` / `no_speech`: final, from the station's whisper; `remote`: the hub is to transcribe it (see `transcript_pending`); `off`: kept, not transcribed; `skipped`: whisper was busy, it may be caught up later; `error`: whisper failed; `pending`: not transcribed yet (an alarm). The hub takes a missing one as `done`.

unit.description: Who talked, as the station names them: an alias, a tag or the radio id, joined with ", "; "" when not known. An MDC-1200 emergency adds ` EMERGENCY` to the name.

talkgroup.description: The P25 talkgroup number; null on an FM or airband channel. With `system` set it is that system's number, never the county's.

rig.description: The unit the station's registry gives the radio; "" when unknown. The hub writes its own registry's answer over it ("" for another P25 system's).

radio_id.description: The radio id(s) as decoded (P25 unit id, MDC-1200, FleetSync), joined with ", "; "" when none.

raw.description: The transcript as speech-to-text wrote it; "" when none. The hub takes it as the row's text.

confidence.description: The model's confidence in `raw`, 0 to 1; null without one.

model.description: The model that wrote `raw` (a file name), or in its place why there are no words (`pool`, `weak signal (carrier 2.0 dB): not transcribed`, `<model> (skipped: busy ...)`): at most 200 characters.

stt.description: Which engine the hub is to add. "": none; `aws`: the hub's Amazon Transcribe writes the text (with `transcript_pending`); `both`: the hub adds Amazon Transcribe's text as the alternative.

transcript_pending.description: Present only when the station did not transcribe it and the hub is to: `aws` (Amazon Transcribe on the clip) or `pool` (the hub's speech-to-text pool, in the class `stt_class`). The hub takes any other value as absent.

stt_wait_s.description: How long it waited in the station's whisper queue, seconds, two decimals; null when it never queued. Present once whisper ran.

stt_run_s.description: How long whisper ran on it, seconds, two decimals. Present once whisper ran.

stt_class.description: The class of the whisper queue it ran in, or (with `transcript_pending` `pool`) the class the pool is to take it in.

stt_prompt_time.description: Whisper's prompt carried the clip's own time. Present once the station's whisper took it.

vocab_v.description: The version of the term list that went into whisper's prompt; "" when none. Present once the station's whisper took it. The hub cuts it to 80 characters.

attach.description: `traffic` only, always there: the station's own choice whether this is our traffic (an FM channel, or a talkgroup its Main switch is on; never another P25 system's). The hub takes it as the row's `ours` on a talkgroup and attaches it to the active incident; a missing one makes the hub decide by its own switches.

prefixItems.description: The P25 radio id, digits as a string; "" when none was decoded.
The alias the system sent for it; "" when none.

items.description: One talker: [radio id, alias]. The hub drops a pair that is not a two-item list.

pairs.description: The P25 talkers of this key-up, for the hub's own registry lookup. `traffic`: null on a channel that is not P25 (and on another P25 system's, whose radios are never looked up). `alarm`: always a list, [] when none.

low_energy.description: FM and airband: the clip has less than the least speech whisper needs. Whisper's judge reads it on the station.

id_note.description: FM: why a key-up has no radio id. Present only when it has none and a reason is known.

emergency.description: The radio's emergency button: P25 (the call's flag) or an MDC-1200 / FleetSync emergency packet. An `alarm` always carries it: false marks a flag the station found stuck (see `flag_stuck`). The hub takes an alarm without it as true.

emergency_via.description: FM: which signalling carried the emergency packet. Present only with an FM emergency.

alarm_key.description: FM: the id of the alarm already raised at the key-up of this carrier (`<label without spaces>-live-<start in ms>`), which this transmission takes over. Present only when there was one.

kept.description: P25: why a call on a talkgroup whose Record switch is off was kept. Present only then.

late.description: P25: true on a call written while sizeup was down and ingested at its next start (#747): it goes to the radio log and speech-to-text like any, no pre-alert hears it, and an emergency still alarms, labelled late. An emergency's alarm mark always carries it (false when live); a transmission only when true.

flag_stuck.description: P25: the emergency flag on this call is one the station found stuck (a radio left in emergency mode, a talkgroup held in emergency): who or what it is stuck on, for people. Present only then; never together with `emergency` true.

evidence.description: P25 emergency: trunk-recorder's own record of the call (its JSON, in its own format, with `file` added and `srcList` / `freqList` cut to 200 entries), kept for audit. Present only with a P25 emergency whose record could be read. Not described here: it is another program's format.

fm.description: False: the clip needs no FM de-emphasis (decoded P25 voice, AM airband). Absent on an FM channel, which is taken as true. Read when the clip is transcribed again.

call_id.description: P25: the id of the whole call this key-up is a piece of (trunk-recorder's call name).

turn.description: P25: which key-up of the call this is, from 0.

mhz.description: Airband: the frequency it was heard on, MHz, four decimals.

carrier_db.description: Airband: the carrier over the noise floor, dB, one decimal.

carrier_dbfs.description: Airband: the carrier's level, dBFS, one decimal. Present when measured.

snr_db.description: Airband: the voice's signal-to-noise ratio, dB, one decimal. Present when measured.

opened.description: Airband: what opened the squelch. Present when measured.

notched_hz.description: Airband: the steady tones notched out of the clip. Present only when there were some.

floor_dbfs.description: Airband: the noise floor it was measured against, dBFS, one decimal. Present when measured.

system.description: Another P25 system's transmission (context: never our traffic, never on an incident, no alarm): that system's short name. Absent on everything else. With it the station holds the event back from a hub that has not said `p25_systems` in its `caps`.

tier.description: Another P25 system's: the tier its talkgroup had when the call was heard.

ours.description: A P25 row is one of ours. Another P25 system's: always false. The county's: set by the station from `attach` as it sends; the hub writes its own from `attach` over it.

source_key.description: Another P25 system's: the row's source, `p25:<system>:<talkgroup>`.

group.description: Another P25 system's: the talkgroup's group in that system's talkgroups file; "" when none.

service_auto.description: Another P25 system's: the service its talkgroups file gives the talkgroup, before any choice by an admin. The hub applies its own admins' choice over it.

service.description: Another P25 system's: the service the station used (the admins' choice it had then, else `service_auto`). The hub reads it only when `service_auto` is missing (an older station).

dept.description: Another P25 system's: the talkgroup's department in that system's talkgroups file; "" when none.

feed_event.title: A feed event
feed_event.description: One event of an external incident source as its adapter hands it over (sizeup/sources/__init__.py FeedEvent.as_dict). The station checks it before it is queued and the hub checks it again (FeedEvent.check): at most 60 units of at most 32 characters, 500 comments, 2000 characters a text, 50 aliases, 16 KiB of `extra`, 256 KiB in all.

source.description: The adapter's id, the same as the event's `source` beside it.

event_id.description: The source's own id of the event, 1 to 64 characters.

type.description: The type of call as the source words it; at most 2000 characters.

location.description: The address as the source words it; at most 2000 characters.

times.description: The event's times by name, each Unix seconds. The names the hub knows today: `dispatched`, `responding`, `on_location`, `en_route_to`, `out_at`, `in_service`.

additionalProperties.description: One unit's times by name, each Unix seconds.

unit_times.description: Each unit's own times, by unit code.

prefixItems.description: When the comment was made, Unix seconds.

closed.description: The source says the event is closed.

extra.description: Anything else the adapter gives, JSON values under text keys, at most 16 KiB as JSON. The hub shows `jurisdiction`, `run_numbers` and `group_units` and keeps the rest.

items.description: Another id of the same event, 1 to 64 characters.

aliases.description: Other event ids of this source that are this event (merged into it).
